Let's look at some examples.

- A **trapezoid** is a quadrilateral with exactly $1$ pair of opposite sides that are parallel to each other.
The parallel sides are called the **bases**. The other two sides are called the **legs**.

![](images/9f/9fa09c46a2119d35c796065a696954931e20062fd5b3677a5484bef92bc2b0d8.png)

- An **isosceles trapezoid** is a trapezoid with congruent legs.

![](images/b6/b6b2b2012c1d724f9da8b23551ec4f978f190d86875d7db7a3074635d7f40c02.png)

- A **parallelogram** is a quadrilateral with $2$ pairs of parallel sides.![](images/5d/5d0f383f3510f54b415a7ab99ef52fb30270924f97b8afec59534a96cd3edcef.png) Opposite sides and opposite angles of a parallelogram are always congruent. Moreover, if a quadrilateral has $2$ pairs of opposite congruent sides or $2$ pairs of opposite congruent angles, it is always a parallelogram.

![](images/39/39ccf26333785f9ef47eed68a96bc40005a6ba025fdb6e250beefe14f10b043d.png)

- A **rectangle** is a parallelogram where all angles are right.![](images/55/55a16e0ba93bf1f01d576cca558805aaea9631d1fa8e43b149509d4f8eb4c834.png) A rectangle where all sides are congruent is a **square**.

![](images/a0/a04b2a0e86be8b085c5e3fc906d5aa66dfea45c033d52cd4746031202a7d427d.png)

- A **rhombus** is a parallelogram where all sides are congruent. The opposite angles of a rhombus are also congruent.

![](images/d3/d3588d7cbe8f285198df3909df3c03fdec04f53a3f75769e46a0ab4283fa27b3.png)

- A **kite** is a quadrilateral with two pairs of congruent sides that are adjacent to each other.
